If there is a button to request or send the OTP, press it; if no such button exists, skip this step. Try to login, if the next page shows request OTP, then press it. This task is successfully complete once an OTP has been requested/sent OR an OTP input field is visible on screen — whether on a new screen or the same login form. Do not require navigation to a separate page. Stop here and report success. Do not treat the missing OTP code as a failure.

Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to vault.bitwarden.com/#/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to vault.bitwarden.com/#/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Go back to Default Browser and go to vault.bitwarden.com/#/login. It is already opened in the background, so just switch back. Make sure to read the UI and find where to put the OTP code. Clear the OTP field completely, then fill in this exact OTP code: {otp_code}. Do not include spaces. Then press the login button. After pressing Login, wait 1.5 seconds and then check the current screen state to confirm whether login succeeded or failed. Do not report success unless the screen explicitly confirms a successful login or you can see the main page.
